title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. These are 1970 'Cristaux' scribbles, from the period of Grothendieck's Montreal lectures on Barsotti–Tate groups and Dieudonné crystals. The page studies p-divisible (formal) groups G_0 over a perfect field k of characteristic p that carry an action of A, the ring of integers of a finite extension K/Q_p with residue degree f. The verso is an unrelated typescript on jets.

Setup. The Dieudonné module of such a group is a module over W(k)⊗_{Z_p}A. It splits along the f embeddings of the residue field F_{p^f} into k as M = ⊕_{ν=0}^{f-1} M_ν. Frobenius gives σ-semilinear maps φ_ν: M_ν → M_{ν+1}.

First part: end of a proposition about the height h, dimension 1 case. The groups are classified by data (π, ν, Ω). Here π is an element playing the role of a Frobenius or Weil-type element, ν is a valuation index, and Ω is an associated K-module or algebra. The claims are:
- Hom(G_0, G'_0) ≠ 0, i.e. G_0 and G'_0 are isogenous, iff π = π'.
- In that case, if ν = ν', then Hom_A(G_0, G'_0) ≅ Hom(Ω', Ω). Note the contravariance, typical of Dieudonné theory.
- If ν > ν', then Hom_A(G_0, G'_0) ≅ π·Hom(Ω', Ω).
This is a Tate/Honda-type statement: isogeny class is determined by the Frobenius element, and the Hom group is an explicit lattice in the Hom of the rational data.

'Rem NB': the general case. Now drop dim = 1 and keep only height h, and classify up to isogeny.
- After inverting p, each M_ν becomes a vector space over K_0, the fraction field of W.
- φ_0, …, φ_{f-2} are isomorphisms, so all M_ν are identified with M_0.
- Hence M ≅ Ω ⊗_K (K ⊗_{Q_p} K_0) for a K-vector space Ω.
- The F-structure is then determined by φ_{f-1}, i.e. by one endomorphism ϖ of Ω, with F_M^f = ϖ ⊗ id_{K_0}.
- So isogeny classes correspond to pairs (Ω, ϖ): a K-linear endomorphism up to conjugacy.

Effectivity. The condition for (Ω, ϖ) to come from an actual group is: ϖ preserves a lattice, and pϖ^{-1} preserves a lattice. In other words, the eigenvalues of ϖ are integral and have p-adic valuation in [0, v(p)]. This is the analogue, for A-modules, of the Manin slope condition 0 ≤ slope ≤ 1.

What it serves. This is the Dieudonné-theoretic classification, up to isogeny, of p-divisible groups with A-action (formal A-modules) over a perfect field. It mirrors the Honda–Tate classification by Frobenius 'Weil numbers'.
errors: The bound 'p ϖ^{-1} laisse invariant un réseau' is correct only if φ_0, …, φ_{f-2} are integral isomorphisms. That holds for strict/special formal A-modules, where A acts on Lie through the structure map. For a general p-divisible group with A-action it holds only up to isogeny, and the effectivity condition should read p^f ϖ^{-1}, i.e. slopes of F^f in [0, f]. For K ramified, the strict condition involves a uniformizer rather than p. Grothendieck's sentence slides between the isogeny statement and the integral statement.

The statement 'si ν > ν', Hom_A ≅ π Hom(Ω', Ω)' depends on conventions from the preceding page, which we do not have, so it cannot be fully checked. The asymmetry (no case ν < ν') suggests the integrality lattice was only worked out in one direction.

The notation M ≅ Ω ⊗_{Q_p} W is inconsistent with the following expression Ω ⊗_K (K ⊗_{Q_p} K_0). As the marginal note indicates, W should be read as the fraction field K_0, and the tensor product should be over K, not Q_p.

ideas.what: Isogeny between p-divisible A-modules over a finite or perfect field holds iff the Frobenius-type invariants π coincide; Hom groups are described as lattices in Hom(Ω', Ω)
ideas.modern_name: Honda–Tate / Tate isogeny theorem for p-divisible groups and formal A-modules over finite fields
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to the Montreal lectures 'Groupes de Barsotti–Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (1970/74), but not this specific statement as far as known

ideas.what: Decomposition of the Dieudonné module of a p-divisible group with O_K-action into eigencomponents M_ν, reducing the structure to M_0 with the f-th power of Frobenius
ideas.modern_name: Eigenspace decomposition for O_K-Dieudonné modules (relative Dieudonné theory, π-divisible modules)

ideas.what: Effectivity criterion: an isocrystal with K-action comes from a group iff ϖ and pϖ^{-1} each preserve a lattice
ideas.modern_name: Slope condition 0 ≤ slopes ≤ 1 (Manin) for effective Dieudonné modules

deep.surprise_reason: This is a competent private working-out of the isogeny classification of p-divisible groups with O_K-action via Dieudonné modules (reduction to (Ω, ϖ) plus the Manin-type effectivity condition). All of it is subsumed by Tate, Honda, Manin and later Drinfeld/Hazewinkel. It is of mild historical interest as evidence that Grothendieck considered formal A-modules around 1970, but nothing here is new.
transcription_corrections: The 'ssi' that the transcription marks as deleted reads like a struck word ('ssi' or 'si'); the logic requires 'iff'.
The line 'M ≅ Ω ⊗_{Q_p} W' is preceded by a crossed-out phrase. In the right-hand side 'Ω ⊗_K (K ⊗_{Q_p} K_0)', the K_0 carries the annotation 'corps des fractions de W'.
'F_M^f = ϖ ⊗_{Q_p} id_{K_0}' should probably read ϖ ⊗_K id, consistent with the right-hand side.
First-case annotation: the handwriting shows a struck 'G_0 = G'_0' after 'si ν = ν''.
